newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 7.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* A two percentage point cut in the central bank's overnight borrowing rate is likely to help Philippine shares vault beyond the 2,700 psychological barrier on Thursday, brokers said.

* "While the magnitude of the cuts are not significant, it sends signals of a stabilising peso-dollar market, hence possibly boosting market sentiment," Sun Hung Kai Securities research head Raul Ruiz said in a report.
The central bank trimmed its closely watched borrowing rate to 18 percent. It also cut its lending rate to 22 percent from 25.
* A BPI Securities Corp study, however, said any uptrend might be capped as the market is still in a consolidation mode.
"Most first half corporate reports (which are generally in line with expectations) have already been released, providing few surprises to prop up the equity market," the report said.
* Brokers see 2,750 points as the next resistance level. The composite index closed higher by 18.59 points, or 0.69 percent, at 2,694.79 points on Wednesday.
* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones jumped 71.77 points to 8,259.31 points.
* The peso closed 28.49 to the dollar vs Tuesday's close of 28.65. The peso has been gaining steadily in recent days albeit amid light turnover.
* The Philippine overnight money dipped to 20.46875 percent from 20.9375.
* Uniwide Holdings Inc says first half profit rises 34 percent to 414 million pesos.
* Alaska Milk Corp says first half net income surges 297 percent to 138 million pesos.
* Philippines' Presidential Commission on Good Government says it will sell its 51 million Manila Electric Co shares to the public before the end of the year.
* The Export-Import Bank of Japan says it has syndicated a $24 million loan to the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co.
* Trans-Asia Oil and Energy Development Corp says it has bought three percent stake in an Indonesian drilling consortium.
* Ayala Corp-led Manila Water Co gets a package of tax and fiscal incentives by the Board of Investments.
* Victorias Milling Co says its net loss in the first nine months of the year amounted to 1.23 billion pesos, higher than the net loss of 60.7 million registered in the same period last year.
